title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 81-82
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 81 to 82 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'तेजोवृषो द्युतिधरः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 81 to 82 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 81 to 82.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 81 to 82** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **तेजोवृषो द्युतिधरः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**तेजोवृषो द्युतिधरः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः । प्रग्रहो निग्रहो व्यग्रो नैकशृङ्गो गदाग्रजः ॥** **चतुर्मूर्तिश्चतुर्बाहुश्चतुर्व्यूहश्चतुर्गतिः । चतुरात्मा चतुर्भावश्चतुर्वेदविदेकपात् ॥**

Radiance is his strength and he bears a shining glory. The best among all who bear weapons is that God of gods. He restrains and he corrects, he stays unshaken, with many horns, the elder brother of Gada. Four forms, four arms, four manifestations and four goals are his. Four aspects of the Self, four sentiments, the knower of all four Vedas, the one who stands on a single foot, is that God of gods.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 81 to 82 mean?
faq.a: Radiance is his strength and he bears a shining glory. The best among all who bear weapons is that God of gods. He restrains and he corrects, he stays unshaken, with many horns, the elder brother of Gada. Four forms, four arms, four manifestations and four goals are his. Four aspects of the Self, four sentiments, the knower of all four Vedas, the one who stands on a single foot, is that God of gods.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
